page: Microsoft Azure E2bs_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance deployed on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The system is driven by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8370C processor clocked at 2.8 GHz, providing two dedicated virtual CPUs mapped to a single physical core via multithreading. Memory is provisioned at 16.0 GB, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Cache resources comprise 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of L3 cache. Supported instruction set extensions include AVX, AVX-512, AVX-512_VNNI, and cryptographic primitives including AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

This server profile includes zero local disk storage and contains no discrete GPU acceleration, directing all persistent and ephemeral input/output operations through attached remote block storage options such as Azure Premium Storage. The instance is also provisioned without complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Benchmark performance aligns with the single physical core configuration: single-threaded metrics maintain average output, achieving 1890.78 in stress-ng and 1623.0 in Geekbench. Conversely, multi-threaded results fall into lower percentiles, as evidenced by a PassMark CPU score of 2986.72 and multi-core Geekbench score of 1880.0. Large-block memory bandwidth measures 15.07 GB/sec for uncached reads and 13.81 GB/sec for writes.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E2bs_v5 provides a cost-effective allocation of RAM without forcing adoption of high core counts. The instance architecture is best matched with memory-demanding but compute-modest applications, such as small caching layers, lightweight relational databases, microservice runtimes, and intermediate ETL staging environments that function adequately within the parameters of remote block storage.
description: Microsoft Azure E2bs_v5 is an entry-level memory-optimized instance operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It is equipped with two dedicated vCPUs derived from a single physical Intel Xeon 8370C core running at 2.8 GHz, paired with 16.0 GB of system memory to achieve an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio. The instance lacks local storage, requiring attached remote block storage, and contains no discrete GPU accelerators or complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Benchmark results indicate balanced single-thread execution with a stress-ng score of 1890.78 and Geekbench single-core score of 1623.0, though multi-core compute and database operations remain limited by the single underlying physical core. Supported by AVX-512 and cryptographic hardware instructions, the E2bs_v5 is architected for small-scale in-memory caches, lightweight database servers, microservices, and memory-dependent enterprise workloads that operate effectively on attached block storage without demanding multi-core parallelism.
